grh_f6b4327eb938191108d2.title: There Is No Such Thing As Luck
paragraphs: Wealthy fashion heir Henry Martin III comes to Dr. Christian miserable with his pampered business life and convinced that what he really needs is honest work on a farm. Christian pairs him with struggling farmer Tim Halsey and daughter Molly: Martin takes over the Halsey farm while the Halseys live in his Chicago apartment, with Martin also paying them a monthly allowance. The arrangement succeeds so well that Martin turns the farm into a profitable operation and wants to keep it, but after nearly a year the Halseys decide to return. When they refuse an extension, Martin threatens to sue Christian for $100,000 over the doctor's guarantee that he could remain. The dispute collapses when Molly reveals that she has used her time in Chicago to study fashion design. Her self-made clothes immediately impress Martin, who forgets the lawsuit and wants her for his firm. Soon afterward Molly writes that she and Martin plan to marry, leaving Christian amused that luck has solved a problem Martin insisted luck did not exist.

Credited performers include Jean Hersholt, Gloria Holden, [[person|bennett-kilpack|Bennett Kilpack]], Burford Hampden, and Eustace Wyatt. Production credits include announcer Andre Baruch.

grh_f60dc2996435fbcf7863.title: The Mc Guffey Connection
paragraphs: Narcotics agent Arnold McGuffey goes to East Africa under cover of running a small school while awaiting word on an opium shipment intended for the heroin trade. The supposed cover operation becomes real as local adults learn to read, write and master practical skills, and McGuffey becomes increasingly determined to give them a genuine education. He renames the school Equatorial University and organizes diplomas, a multi-faith blessing and a graduation ceremony while a female contact keeps him informed about the rerouted shipment. By the end, the drug mission is still ahead of him, but the school has become far more than a disguise.

grh_f6f60373cb8132a11588.title: Susan The Opera Singer
paragraphs: Local singer Susan believes her great chance has arrived when famous opera star Sigrid Holmquist and impresario Otto Kaufman visit Rivers End. Desperate to be heard, Susan even asks Dr. Christian to keep Holmquist from singing at a charity concert when the star seems to be catching a cold, but he refuses to manufacture an opportunity for her. After Holmquist performs brilliantly, Dr. Christian explains that the star once struggled for years through rejection, poor jobs and relentless study before she was ready. Susan accepts that she still has work to do, and Holmquist warmly invites her to come backstage after the next concert, giving her encouragement without pretending success can be rushed.
